reported_claims.text: Hunger is set to worsen significantly in 16 hotspots over the next six months, with the gravest famine threats in Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen.

Chad, Uganda and parts of Southern Africa and Central America were added to the list; Lebanon was removed. Armed conflict drives hunger in 12 of the 16 hotspots and El Nino is a major driver in three of the four new ones.
Famine remains a risk in 13 areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan in Sudan through January 2027.
Humanitarian aid to the five most at-risk countries fell from 5.1 billion dollars to 2 billion dollars between 2022 and 2025.

title: UN agencies warn hunger will worsen in 16 hotspots as conflict and El Nino drive famine risk
summary: A joint FAO and WFP early-warning report released on 27 November 2026 says acute hunger is set to worsen significantly in 16 hotspots between December 2026 and May 2027, up from 13 in June. Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen face the gravest famine threats. Conflict drives hunger in 12 of the 16 hotspots and El Nino in three of the four new ones, while humanitarian funding for the most at-risk countries has fallen sharply.
impact_assessment: Potential: famine conditions in several conflict zones, increased displacement and migration pressure, and greater instability where food insecurity overlaps with armed conflict.
priority_rationale: MODERATE: an authoritative UN forward-looking warning covering multiple conflict zones; not a single acute event.
